newsitem.title: GERMANY: CompuServe German chief leaves firm. [CORRECTED 15:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CompuServe German chief leaves firm. [CORRECTED 15:38 GMT]

text.p: Online service provider CompuServe Corp said the head of its German operation, who has been targeted in a crackdown on Internet pornography, would leave the company.
Felix Somm, who was charged in April with distributing banned materials in Germany, was leaving CompuServe to start his own business, the company said in a statement.

"We regret losing Felix Somm, but we respect his decision to leave CompuServe GmbH to found his own company," Jerry Roest (corrects spelling of his surname from Roast), CompuServe's general manager for Europe said.
Somm was charged with disseminating child pornography, Nazi writings and other material that glorify violence that are banned in Germany but could be found on parts of the Internet called newsgroups.

Authorities said Somm knew the materials were accessible in Germany via CompuServe and did little to block access. Prosecutors are waiting for a court to decide if there is enough evidence for the case to proceed. No date has been set.
Previously, Compuserve said it would vigorously fight the charges and predicted they would eventually be dropped.
Eva Preuss, general manager of CompuServe GmbH, would run the unit until a successor to Somm is found, the company said.
